Contaminated water spread dysentery, typhoid, and other waterborne diseases constantly.
People were sick so often, they thought it was just… normal. Some historians estimate that in
crowded, medieval towns, the average person had intestinal parasites their entire life
and never knew it. It was a system so efficient at spreading disease that it killed tens of
millions of people across Europe. And nobody connected the water to the deaths for another
500 years. After you finish your heroic trip to the bucket, your stomach still hurts. It doesn't
stop. It growls. It burns. It feels like something inside you is trying to tear its way out.
